subject: Operational attribution proposal — Private edge handoff (EdgeCore)
messages:
From: David Chen <dchen@edgecore.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: SLA Legal <legal@edgecore.io>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private edge handoff — attribution for availability/latency

Hi Jonas,

Quick note following our run-through yesterday. We're planning to cut traffic to Redwood's private edge collector on Aug 9 as part of our migration to the new customer-controlled NAT appliances. Because this path will traverse our own NAT + peering, our security team expects clarity on how availability and tail-latency will be attributed in the event of an incident.

Specifically: if there is a customer-operated edge or peering fault (packet loss, NAT misconfiguration, transit flaps) that results in increased p50/p95 token latency or degraded throughput to the Redwood Private control plane, would Redwood accept an operational attribution that absolves Redwood of the availability SLA for that window, provided EdgeCore can produce:
- evidence of edge-level packet captures or router logs showing errors during the window
- timing correlation to our BGP/peering changes
- confirmation that the gateway was under our administrative control at the time

I've attached a simple infra map to show the handoff. Our legal and ops folks want to embed a short attribution matrix in the SOW instead of a full carve-out appendix if possible.

Can you point me to the internal contact who would accept this evidence and the format Redwood prefers? Also, any recommended wording for a tight operational attribution clause would help accelerate our procurement.

Thanks,
David
David Chen
Head of Platform Ops | EdgeCore Systems
attachments: edgecore-infra-map.pdf (see attached)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, dchen@edgecore.io
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private edge handoff — attribution for availability/latency

Looping in infra/ops and compliance to scope the acceptance criteria David requested. Short answers up front: yes, we can accept customer-provided evidence for attribution, but we need a bounded set of artifacts and timelines and a short handoff clause to include in the SOW.

Karthik / Mina / Naomi — can you propose an evidence checklist and a one-paragraph clause that:
- limits attribution to incidents where the customer-controlled hop is the root cause
- requires the customer to produce logs/pcaps within 5 business days of the incident
- allows Redwood to validate the artifacts and to run our own correlation before granting an SLA credit or excusing availability targets

David — thanks for the infra map. If you can include sample filenames or the typical retention window for your router logs that will help.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, david.chen@edgecore.io
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private edge handoff — attribution for availability/latency

Hi team — draft below. Kept deliberately narrow to avoid open-ended carve-outs. Feedback welcome.

--- begin proposed clause ---
Operational Attribution for Customer-Controlled Edge
If Customer-managed edge infrastructure, peering, or NAT appliances ("Customer Edge") is the proximate cause of a degradation in Redwood's Service availability or latency SLOs, Customer may submit an attribution request. An attribution request must include the following artifacts within five (5) business days of the incident end time: (i) time-synchronised packet captures (pcap) or router/system logs covering the impacted interval; (ii) BGP/peering session state changes and timestamps; (iii) configuration change records and change control ticket IDs; and (iv) the Customer Edge contact responsible for the maintenance window.

Redwood will validate the artifacts and may perform independent correlation using Redwood telemetry. If Redwood reasonably concludes (a) the provided artifacts demonstrate that the Customer Edge was the proximate cause and (b) Redwood's infrastructure did not contribute to the failure, Redwood will treat the incident as a Customer-attributed event for purposes of availability and tail-latency SLOs and will not apply a Service-level credit for that event. Redirected logging and packet evidence produced by the Customer must include sufficient context to map to Redwood request/response traces (request IDs, timestamps, source/destination IPs).

Limitations: Attribution requests will not apply to third-party transit failures outside the Customer Edge boundary unless the Customer provides verifiable transit provider evidence. Attribution requests may be rejected if artifacts are incomplete or if Redwood cannot reproduce the correlation within a reasonable technical window.
--- end proposed clause ---

Proposed attachments: a short template evidence checklist we can attach to the SOW (I can generate v1). Also note: we should require time-synchronisation (NTP) on customer devices.

Mina / Naomi — operationally, we should confirm the internal owner who will review artifacts and the expected SLAs for Redwood's validation timeline (I recommend 3 business days to triage and 10 business days to complete correlation). If we accept this, we'll add a one-line reference in the SOW and a short appendix with the checklist.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Infrastructure Reliability | Redwood Inference
attachments: sro-claue-draft.txt (internal)

Jonas / Karthik,

This is excellent — thanks for the clear, narrow language. EdgeCore is happy to accept the proposed checklist as the evidence bundle and we'll confirm retention windows so pcaps/logs are available for at least 14 days post-incident. We'll also include the NTP requirement in our maintenance guidance.

Next steps from our side: legal will incorporate the one-line reference into the SOW and attach the checklist as Appendix B. Ops will share sample router log extracts and a test pcap from our lab to validate mapping to Redwood request IDs.

If you can provide the short validation SLA (3 business days triage / 10 business days correlation) in writing, we can lock the wording and move to a countersign in the next SOW draft.

Best,
David
